definition: The gradual unravelling of a machine’s grip on a long task; the point at which instructions given early no longer hold.
etymology: From thread (Old English þrǣd, ‘twisted filament’, adopted for conversations) + fray (ultimately Latin fricare, ‘to rub’ — cloth wearing thin). Two weaving words.
in_use: Forty turns in, the tone brief was gone — classic threadfray.
the_case: It names the most common failure a promptwright manages, in the register of cloth and loom rather than jargon.
seo_title: threadfray: when a machine loses its grip on a long task
seo_description: The gradual unravelling of a machine’s grip on a long task: the point at which instructions given early no longer hold.
